To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed method achieves a dense semantic classification of weed and crops with multispectral images and MAV.

1) the use of multispectral images for weed detection and classification is feasible; 2) the use of a cascaded encoder–decoder network for multispectral image classification is effective for dense semantic segmentation; 3) the use of the normalized difference vegetation indices as a distinguishable features for weed classification is promising; and 4) the use of embedded GPU for real-time weed detection and classification on an MAV is feasible.
we present the first dense semantic weed classification using a multispectral MAV system and a novel dataset that can be used for future work.
